evidence: Scope: three scored dimensions use mode="batched", aggregation="weighted_mean" (functional 44 criteria, polish 5, visual 5); the gates render/constraints use aggregation="all_pass" and are exempt. Each scored prompt carries explicit independence and continue-after-failure wording: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature'; polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' Supporting wording in all three: line 7 'If a feature does not work as delivered, give that criterion its lowest score ... state what you observed, and move on'; the NOT EXERCISED paragraph (functional:61, polish:26, visual:20) zeroes only 'the unobserved outcome' and says 'Preserve every completed independent observation'; 'Report every step' makes a skipped step fail 'that criterion' only. No stop-at-first-failure, abort, halt or skip-remaining wording exists in any scored prompt, judge.toml criterion or app_context.md (grep for stop|first fail|abort|halt|remaining criteri|skip the rest returned no such hit). The only dimension-wide zero is the in-dimension browser gate (functional:13, polish:12, visual:12), which is row 29's legitimate gate, not a cascade between criteria. Criterion-level cross-references reinforce independence rather than chaining: e.g. hro_job_open 'graded only in hro_interview_full and the manager rows'; the 403/401-status row 'a replay that was accepted is deducted only in its own row'; T fallback 'If that card never appears for Tomas (graded only in hro_candidate_linked), use his seeded Data Analyst conversation'; U fallback 'if Tomas cannot send, which is graded only in hro_msg_exchange, Mei Lin sends'; polish live-thread 'Mei Lin if Noor cannot send; that is graded in Functional'; hro_activity_refusals is the sole owner of refused-action Activity lines (functional:27). Colderwater lessons checked for every instance bearing on this row: L6 checker-not-fixer present in all three scored prompts (line 7) and its 'move on' supports continuing; L9 report-every-step present in all three and scoped per criterion; L11/L4 judge/tool failures and gates handled per-outcome (NOT EXERCISED) rather than zeroing siblings; L16 no double penalty present in functional:31 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row', polish:24 and visual:14. Matches the template's intent (template scored prompts: 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'). Adversarial tries: (a) a conforming app with one failing row (e.g. stale-move refusal broken) - prompt wording forbids using that verdict against other rows and requires continuing, so siblings are not zeroed; (b) a broken app passing because of this wording - not applicable, independence wording cannot itself credit a dead feature; refusal rows still need their own positive control (functional:13). Residual observation for other rows (not a row-38 wording defect): if job opening fails completely, the 'new job of your own' fallback is impossible and no explicit seeded-job fallback is named, so most board protocols would become unobservable; that is a precondition-concentration question for rows 37/40, noted here for reconciliation. This is a source/wording review; check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed and no configured judge run was examined for whether the judge actually continued after failures.
